title: Cohesive Conversations: Enhancing Authenticity in Multi-Agent Simulated Dialogues
publication_evidence: Official OpenReview record and published conference PDF
decision_reason: Multiple agents exchange dialogue and memory but the endpoint is dialogue authenticity and factual consistency without an adversary or security contract.
metric_and_denominator: Dialogue quality and error rates over generated conversations; no security denominator.
evidence_locators: Published PDF pp. 1-2 Abstract and Introduction; Sections 3-5 and Tables 1-4.
limitations: Interaction-dependent reliability work rather than direct security evidence.

title: Towards Collaborative Intelligence: Propagating Intentions and Reasoning for Multi-Agent Coordination with Large Language Models
publication_evidence: No archival publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: The paper studies learned communication and coordination performance; it does not define an adversary or violated security property.
metric_and_denominator: Task performance and grounding accuracy over benchmark tasks.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-3 system and contribution; Section 4 and PDF pp. 6-8 evaluation.
limitations: Coordination performance is relevant background but not security evidence.

title: Multi-Agent Large Language Models for Conversational Task-Solving
publication_evidence: No archival publication located; the accessed work is an arXiv thesis-style manuscript.
decision_reason: The paper measures task performance and alignment collapse in prolonged discussion but does not specify a security adversary or security contract.
metric_and_denominator: Accuracy and task-specific quality metrics; safety discussion is not an adversarial security denominator.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-5 scope and claimed safety concerns; Sections 4-5 and PDF pp. 14-29 evaluation.
limitations: Useful for collective reliability and alignment context; security is not the primary contribution.

title: CoopetitiveV: Leveraging LLM-powered Coopetitive Multi-Agent Prompting for High-quality Verilog Generation
publication_evidence: Official ICML 2025 virtual page lists an MAS workshop poster rather than a main-track archival paper.
decision_reason: The agents generate and correct Verilog; the endpoint is functional correctness rather than a security property.
metric_and_denominator: Pass and correctness metrics over Verilog benchmarks.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-3 architecture; PDF pp. 5-8 evaluation.
limitations: Error propagation and correction are reliability concerns absent an adversary.

title: CodeCoR: An LLM-Based Self-Reflective Multi-Agent Framework for Code Generation
publication_evidence: The v2 revision is post-cutoff; no archival publication was used for this decision.
decision_reason: The multi-agent workflow improves code correctness and quality without an adversarial or security endpoint.
metric_and_denominator: Pass@1 CodeBLEU and functional correctness over code-generation datasets.
evidence_locators: v1 PDF pp. 1-3 workflow; Sections 4-5 and v1 PDF pp. 6-11 evaluation and threats to validity.
limitations: Only the pre-cutoff v1 supports the frozen corpus decision.

title: When Persuasion Overrides Truth in Multi-Agent LLM Debates: Introducing a Confidence-Weighted Persuasion Override Rate (CW-POR)
publication_evidence: No archival publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: A deliberately incorrect advocate attempts to override a truthful agent through debate and the central endpoint is collective decision integrity.
metric_and_denominator: CW-POR over eligible debate instances where the neutral agent begins correct and is exposed to a persuasive incorrect advocate.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-3 threat motivation and metric; Sections 3-5 and PDF pp. 4-8 setup and results; PDF p. 9 limitations.
limitations: Single-turn synthetic debate and confidence proxies limit external validity.

title: Debate Only When Necessary: Adaptive Multiagent Collaboration for Efficient LLM Reasoning
publication_evidence: No archival main-track publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: The paper optimizes debate accuracy and model-call efficiency and does not evaluate a security adversary or property.
metric_and_denominator: Accuracy and average agent calls over reasoning benchmarks.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-3 method; PDF pp. 4-9 results and limitations.
limitations: Adaptive communication is architectural context rather than security evidence.

title: Revisiting Multi-Agent Debate as Test-Time Scaling: A Systematic Study of Conditional Effectiveness
publication_evidence: Official ICML 2025 virtual page lists an MAS workshop paper; no main-track archival record was found.
decision_reason: The safety experiments show debate-dependent changes in jailbreak attack success but security is one task family inside a broader test-time scaling study and the threat model is thin.
metric_and_denominator: Attack success rate over adversarial safety prompts with outcomes aggregated across debate rounds and configurations.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-4 scope; Sections 4-5 and PDF pp. 7-10 safety results; Appendix safety metric definition at PDF pp. 17-18.
limitations: Security findings should be extracted at claim level and not used to classify the entire paper as core security.

title: SentinelAgent: Graph-based Anomaly Detection in Multi-Agent Systems
publication_evidence: No archival publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: The defense models dynamic agent-execution graphs to detect prompt manipulation collusion and latent exploit paths that are defined across interacting agents.
metric_and_denominator: Detection and mitigation outcomes in two framework case studies; denominators and per-case metrics require claim-level extraction.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-4 threat model and graph design; Sections 5-6 and PDF pp. 5-9 defense and case studies; PDF p. 9 limitations.
limitations: Two case studies and a preprint-only evidence base limit generalization.

title: Chasing Moving Targets with Online Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Safer Language Models
publication_evidence: Official ICML 2025 virtual page lists an MAS workshop paper; later revisions are post-cutoff.
decision_reason: Attacker and defender are alternating roles in a self-play training procedure for one protected language model rather than separately addressable deployed agent cores.
metric_and_denominator: Safety benchmark scores and attacker success over generated red-team interactions.
evidence_locators: v1 PDF pp. 1-5 formulation; Sections 4-5 and v1 PDF pp. 5-10 evaluation; appendix in v1 PDF.
limitations: Directly relevant to self-play safety training but outside the strict deployed multi-agent boundary.

title: SAFEFLOW: A Principled Protocol for Trustworthy and Transactional Autonomous Agent Systems
publication_evidence: No archival publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: The protocol enforces provenance-aware information flow and transactional coordination across concurrent agents under adversarial inputs.
metric_and_denominator: Security and reliability outcomes across 440 adversarial task variants plus concurrent multi-agent evaluations; each metric requires claim-level denominator extraction.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-6 system and threat motivation; PDF pp. 6-10 benchmark and results; Appendix PDF pp. 13-20 IFC model and invariants.
limitations: The benchmark combines security reliability and task-success endpoints; it should not be summarized with one aggregate ASR.

title: 1-2-3 Check: Enhancing Contextual Privacy in LLM via Multi-Agent Reasoning
publication_evidence: The paper identifies IASEAI 2026 but no indexed archival proceedings record was located; status remains conservative.
decision_reason: Specialized extractor checker and executor agents regulate contextual information flow and topology ablations show how upstream errors become downstream privacy leakage.
metric_and_denominator: Private-information leakage and public-information omission per benchmark item under single-agent two-agent and three-agent configurations.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-4 motivation and architecture; PDF pp. 4-10 setup results and topology analysis; Appendix PDF pp. 14-21 prompts and ablations.
limitations: Privacy evaluation has no malicious member adversary but directly measures confidentiality failure caused by interaction structure.

title: The Sum Leaks More Than Its Parts: Compositional Privacy Risks and Mitigations in Multi-Agent Collaboration
publication_evidence: No archival publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: An adversary composes individually limited disclosures from multiple agents to infer a protected secret and the paper evaluates coordinated defenses.
metric_and_denominator: Adversarial secret-inference success over synthetic scenarios with balanced-outcome and benign-task trade-off measures.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-4 threat and leakage definition; Sections 3-5 and PDF pp. 4-10 attack defense and results; PDF pp. 12-13 limitations.
limitations: Synthetic data and sanitization assumptions constrain deployment claims.

title: VeriMoA: A Mixture-of-Agents Framework for Spec-to-HDL Generation
publication_evidence: The PDF names MLSys 2026 but no official proceedings record was located in the formality check.
decision_reason: The framework targets HDL correctness and token efficiency without a security adversary or security endpoint.
metric_and_denominator: Pass@1 and token consumption over HDL-generation benchmarks.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-4 framework; Sections 4-5 and PDF pp. 8-12 evaluation.

title: Maestro: Learning to Collaborate via Conditional Listwise Policy Optimization for Multi-Agent LLMs

decision_reason: The paper trains collaborative reasoning and credit assignment for benchmark accuracy rather than a security property.

evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-6 method; PDF pp. 6-9 results; Appendix PDF pp. 15-20 additional evaluation.

title: WOLF: Werewolf-based Observations for LLM Deception and Falsehoods
publication_evidence: Official NeurIPS 2025 virtual page lists a Multi-Turn Interactions workshop poster.
decision_reason: The benchmark measures deception and peer detection but deception is induced by legitimate game roles rather than a security violation against a protected system.
metric_and_denominator: Statement-level deception frequency and detection metrics across game runs and roles.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-3 benchmark motivation and setup; Sections 4-5 and PDF pp. 4-9 measurement and results.
limitations: Useful dual-use evidence for deception and detection; the game-defined objective prevents automatic strict-core inclusion.

title: Agent Drift: Quantifying Behavioral Degradation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems Over Extended Interactions
publication_evidence: No archival publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: The paper uses synthetic longitudinal degradation to study performance and monitoring without an adversary or direct security property.
metric_and_denominator: Task completion accuracy calibration and intervention requirements over simulated interaction rounds.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-3 model and synthetic setup; PDF pp. 4-9 metrics and results; PDF p. 10 limitations.
limitations: Synthetic labels and conceptual degradation make this adjacent reliability evidence.

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
publication_evidence: No archival publication located in the formality check.
decision_reason: The paper defines harmful multi-agent market collusion and evaluates an external governance graph that detects contains and records coordinated behavior.
metric_and_denominator: Run-level collusion tier and market-structure metrics across governance regimes and model configurations.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-4 scope; Sections 3-4 and PDF pp. 7-17 governance contract and experiment; PDF pp. 18-21 results and limitations.
limitations: Economic collusion is a domain-specific security and governance endpoint and evidence remains preprint-only.

title: Taming Various Privilege Escalation in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Mandatory Access Control Framework
publication_evidence: The manuscript contains a placeholder conference line and no archival publication was located.
decision_reason: An untrusted peer can exploit a benign agent as a confused deputy to perform actions outside the authorized privilege set and SEAgent enforces mandatory access control across communication flows.
metric_and_denominator: Privilege-escalation attack success and utility or overhead over AgentDojo API-Bank and multi-agent AWS scenarios; denominators require per-table extraction.
evidence_locators: PDF pp. 1-6 definitions threat model and confused-deputy attack; Sections 5-7 and PDF pp. 7-13 defense and evaluation; Appendix PDF pp. 16-24 scenarios and prompts.
limitations: The paper mixes single-agent and multi-agent evaluations and remains a preprint.
